relevant_findings: Slab doors can often be sanded efficiently using power sanding for large flat areas, but edges and details still require hand work.
Panel and French doors typically require hand sanding on routed profiles and controlled edge burn to prevent beading and improve adhesion.
Louvers have disproportionate labor due to geometry; finish defects are more likely and may require additional inspection and correction.
Occupied environments significantly increase protection/containment needs, especially if spraying is chosen.
condition_drivers: Existing coating hardness and adhesion (bond test failures drive primer and prep escalation).
Edge integrity (crisp 90s cause beading; damage requires feathering and fill).
Contamination level (hand oils, cooking grease, smoke residue).
Hardware complexity (hinges/handles/knobs; paintable hinge swaps change SOP).
quality_differences: QL-3: Standard prep + standard acrylic enamel system; single inspection pass is typical.
QL-4: Higher-performing enamel system; additional inspection/repair pass; stricter sanding between coats where needed.
QL-5: Premium system; multi-stage finishing discipline and additional inspections; louvers at QL-5 may require not-to-exceed authorization.
failure_modes: Edge beading/bridging on crisp edges without burn/sanding.
Adhesion failure over glossy/hard enamel without degloss and bond strategy.
Overspray contamination (occupied spaces) without containment and proper masking.
Runs/sags on louvers or French muntins due to geometry and over-application.
notes_for_materials_manager: Default doors/trim fine finish: QL-3 acrylic enamel; QL-4 modified urethane; QL-5 premium (e.g., Gallery-style) with clear coat option.
Louvers likely need conservative waste factors and additional consumables due to rework risk.
notes_for_sop_librarian: Model 'edge burn' as an explicit task for panel/french/louvered profiles.
Quality expressed via rounds: sanding rounds, inspection rounds, repair rounds.
French door glass protection should be modular (mask lites vs cut-in).
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Rates should be per side (EA) for doors; jamb sets are per opening (EA).
Louvers need lower production, especially at QL-5; consider an escalation note or not-to-exceed pattern.
assumptions: This draft does not include numeric rates; rates require field calibration.
uncertainties: Exact louver geometry variation across door brands can change prep and application time significantly.
Client acceptance thresholds for cut-in vs masked glass can vary and affect SOP selection.
